A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 20 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support comparison. The original material can be matched to its retained or expanded counterparts.

before.justification: v1 reports original stratified analyses of human and machine judgments on SummEval, SNLI, MNLI and MT-Bench, together with synthetic-label simulations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original analyses and adds further stratified results, analyses of three additional datasets, and numerical and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: Uncertainty stratification, binned JSD and perception charts retain the same procedures. The executable logic of the binned-JSD implementation is unchanged; the added walkthrough and simulation code document existing procedures.

E1.justification: Appendix A.11 adds Topical Chat evaluations of understandability and knowledge use, QAGS factual-consistency evaluation, and DICES conversational-safety evaluation. These substantially broaden the represented data and task coverage beyond the retained summarization, NLI and preference experiments.

E2.justification: Corresponding existing experiments retain their comparator membership. The new toy comparison uses the already evaluated Krippendorff, Spearman and Kendall metrics against binned JSD. Llama-3-70B supplies labels for the added case study rather than introducing a competing method against the proposed evaluation approach.

E3.justification: The added case study uses Llama-3-70B and dataset-specific agreement partitions, including DICES with 100–150 human annotations per item. A.12 introduces a controlled three-item comparison of constructed predictors. Existing prompts, decoding settings and sampling procedures are unchanged; fuller reporting of existing strata does not establish that those experiments were redesigned.

E4.justification: Tables 5–6 extend the uncertainty analyses with previously unreported SummEval and MT-Bench strata. A.11 examines class imbalance and stratification on additional data; A.12 tests how collapsing human labels affects metric rankings; A.13 adds SNLI disagreement examples under both unanimous and divided human judgments. These substantially expand the supporting analyses.

E5.justification: The reported 20 machine annotations per example and existing plots with error bars are retained. v2 adds no seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or explanation of uncertainty estimation. Additional annotation counts and small-partition cautions do not constitute new statistical reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results, but Tables 5–6 add strata and Table 8 adds substantial new dataset results. Table 10 reports toy-example binned-JSD scores of 0.56 and 0.65. Some overlapping appendix entries disagree with retained results: G-Eval's relevance H′M alpha at PA<60% is 0.22 in Table 5 versus 0.09 in Table 2, without an explained setting change.

T1.justification: A.12 adds a concrete counterexample showing that comparison against median human labels can give equal or higher correlation to predictions outside the corresponding human label choices. Existing mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(3) remain unchanged; no new theorem or general proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract drops v1's explicit assertion that machine-human correlation declines as human labels become more consistent, focusing instead on its shortfall relative to human-human correlation. The three central contributions—stratification, binned JSD and perception charts—retain their scope.

C2.justification: The additions discuss small-sample exceptions, interpret Topical Chat's divergent metrics through class imbalance, and identify persistent difficulty on DICES. A.12 explicitly acknowledges that validating a metric, including binned JSD, requires independent knowledge of predictor quality. The existing discussion and item-level aggregation limitation are retained.

D1.justification: A.10 supplies simulation-data generators, disclosing 200 binary and 600 ordinal items and their label construction. A.7 adds a worked binned-JSD calculation and clarifies input documentation. A.11 identifies the preprocessed data source and dataset characteristics. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the original implementations.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bavaresco et al.'s evaluation study, the Topical Chat, QAGS and DICES source references, and ten Hove et al. on reliability coefficients. These support the added analyses and metric discussion; the central novelty positioning, including the comparison with cumulative JSD, remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Local revisions clarify uncertainty proportions, notation and captions, and add appendix cross-references and explanatory material. The header changes from conference-paper wording to 'Preprint'. Most existing prose and the main section structure remain intact; the scientific additions do not constitute a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The appendix gains expanded stratification tables, dataset and case-study tables, worked-example tables, and tables displaying individual SNLI judgments. Figure 7 is relocated and resized alongside the expanded material. These substantially extend the evidence displays, while the original plots and main table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 already contained the central evidence and metric implementation. v2 improves scrutiny and usability through fuller strata, broader evaluation coverage, concrete counterexamples, and simulation and calculation guidance. These provide a limited net quality gain, tempered by unexplained discrepancies between newly added H′-based appendix scores and the retained main-text tables.
